adversarial_probes.scenario: Positive control: submit -> approveL1 -> approveL2 by THREE DISTINCT actors (alice/bob/carol)
adversarial_probes.expected: all three pass (SoD not over-strict), 3 actor_event rows
adversarial_probes.note: confirms the guard is not pathologically over-blocking a legitimate multi-actor approval chain

adversarial_probes.scenario: A submit on_behalf_of B; then B approves directly
adversarial_probes.expected: submit attributed to principal B via COALESCE(on_behalf_of,actor); B's later approve collides (DSoD-1) -> denied sod_violation
adversarial_probes.note: matches spec 3.2 — delegated submit's principal is B; no COALESCE collision-with-self loophole. Only the submit row persists (1).

adversarial_probes.scenario: Actor with NO effective assignment (confirmed_by NULL proposal) in a static-SoD constraint
adversarial_probes.expected: static conflict does NOT fire (DAO returns [] effective assignments) -> approve passes (grant permitting)
adversarial_probes.note: matches spec 3.1 / AC-3 — effectiveness filter is the DAO's job; a proposal is inert at action-time.

adversarial_probes.scenario: Guarded approve, deps.sod + guardCtx present, but the injected ledger reader THROWS on every method
adversarial_probes.expected: fail-closed -> denied sod_violation, ZERO actor_event rows
adversarial_probes.note: matches NF-3 — unreadable ledger can never PROVE SoD-clean; evaluateSod try/catch + resolver try/catch both deny.

adversarial_probes.scenario: Repeated IDENTICAL passing guarded approve (same principal, same level)
adversarial_probes.expected: second call still passes; writer appends a SECOND row (append-only, no silent dedup)
adversarial_probes.note: legal per AC-5 ('same principal repeating the same level do not collide') + AC-13 append-only. The ledger is append-only by construction; dedup is NOT in the contract and correctly absent. The operation genuinely repeated, so a second row is honest.

adversarial_probes.scenario: Human/read path single-projection: resolveHandle (op=read) vs the approve entrypoint
adversarial_probes.expected: resolveHandle never enters step 3.6 and never appends; the ONLY approve entrypoint is resolveFor(op=approve) which fail-closes without guardCtx
adversarial_probes.note: matches AC-18 — one decision core (resolveFor); resolveHandle is a read-only facade over it; there is no second un-guarded projection a human approve could slip through.

friction.summary: Pre-existing db-suite cross-file concurrency flake (NOT a T-0032 defect): ci/checks/db runs files in parallel forks against ONE shared Postgres. On a FRESH DB the default-parallel `npm run fitness:db` can intermittently fail AC-4/FF-CT4 (cross_tenant.test.ts DELETE-count race seeded by a sibling file). Verified green 225/225 with --no-file-parallelism and on a 2nd run vs a non-empty DB. T-0032's seedSodConstraint touches only sod_constraint, so it cannot cause the application-row race. Real CI (fresh per-run Postgres, default forks) CAN go intermittently red on this path. Candidate harness fix (separate task, dev-tracked as T-0062): fileParallelism:false or per-file tenant-id namespacing for the db suite.

R-1 stale-base artifact (reviewer-flagged, independently confirmed): cross_tenant.test.ts has a duplicate empIdA/empIdB key (lines 360-361) introduced by 8a449007 (T-0022 BUILD), NOT by this T-0032 coder. esbuild emits 'Duplicate key' warnings on every fitness:db run; harmless at runtime, NOT type-checked (tsconfig include excludes ci/checks). Canonical dev fix b32d403 already de-duplicated it; the orchestrator's rebase onto dev resolves it.

Integration honesty (D-056): the SoD guard branch in resolveFor (step 3.6/6.5) is REAL and reachable — exercised end-to-end through the actual resolveFor/makeGrantResolver entrypoints by 30 unit + 7 adversarial tests (not a mock of the resolver). BUT it is not yet wired into a running request path: (a) deps.sod is never injected by a production caller, and (b) flowable-client.ts references resolveFor only as `void resolveFor;` (a structural FF-G3 grep-satisfier with the explicit comment 'no runtime auth call yet (T-0068)'). This is HONESTLY scoped, not a hidden stub: spec 6 + ADR 10/2.1 explicitly defer the Postgres SodSource/reader/writer DAO to T-0053 and the engine-side guarded caller to T-0028/T-0068. T-0032's owned boundary (gateway guard + writer + ports + migrations + in-memory impl) is complete and tested. Recorded so the orchestrator tracks that SoD is not yet enforced on a live transition until T-0053 (DAO) + T-0068 (lifecycle wiring) land.

Surfaced honestly by analyst+architect, confirmed by reviewer: T-0032 expanded beyond 'implement the 3 reader stubs' to also OWN the guarded-transition writer (appendActorEvent) + the FO-T0019-1 no-decrement debt, because the guarded class cannot record its act without the writer (the writer was tagged 'T-0021/E4.2' with no T-0021 ownership).
